newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Sept 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Sept 25.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The western police district director Superintendent Avelino Razon jr has ordered his 11 station commanders to wage an all-out war against criminals in Manila. (MANILA BULLETIN)

- A transport operators union has called on jeepney (mini bus) and bus drivers to strike on Wednesday to demand a roll back in petrol prices which were raised last month. The government said the strike would have little impact as it was arranging for 100 buses to ferry people if necessary. (MANILA BULLETIN)

- The Philippine National Police, troubled by allegations of corruption and criminal involvement of its officers and men, is seeking the services of a public relations outfit to refurbish its image. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)

- A ranking leader of the House of Representatives on Tuesday confirmed reports a signature campaign to amend the Constitution through people's initiative was being undertaken by an influential political group. (MANILA STANDARD)

- The Philippine National Bank (PNB) and a consortium of U.S. and Japanese investors led by businessman Ramon Jacinto finalized on Monday the sale of a PNB-owned prime plot of land in Makati for 3.7 billion pesos. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)

- Subic Bay Metropolitan Authority said its board of directors had again selected Hutchison Ports Philippines Ltd as the winning bidder to develop a container port terminal. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)

- The Philippine government and the International Monetary Fund have agreed to review the preferential tax treatment on foreign currency deposit units (FDCU) in light of the increasing shift from peso-denominated lending to FDCU lending. (THE BUSINESS DAILY)

- New listings and entry of foreign funds propelled the local stock market's capitalisation to 2.082 trillion pesos in August, but continued growth largely hinged on reforms, Philippine Stock Exchange president Eduardo de los Angeles said. (THE BUSINESS DAILY)
- Westmont Bank, a private commercial bank, plans to go public next year to boost its capital base, Westmont Bank President Edgardo Espiritu said. (THE MANILA CHRONICLE)
